summary.whatChanges: The ETag middleware now trims whitespace around each entry when parsing the `If-None-Match` header, so tags with optional whitespace before the comma (allowed by RFC 9110) are matched. A test covers a list with spaces on both sides of a separator.
behaviorChanges: Requests sending `If-None-Match: "a" , "b"` (space before the comma) now match and return 304 Not Modified instead of a full 200 response.
Leading/trailing whitespace around any entry in the If-None-Match list is ignored during comparison.
risks: Clients that previously received fresh 200 bodies for such headers now get 304, which could surface stale-cache bugs on the client side.
Trimming is whitespace-only and does not handle quoted values containing commas, so malformed headers are still split naively.
